contexts.text: Curtains and cords () = spiritual things from celestial ones.
They let down small cords. HH 335:2. SE 235.
(The correspondence of cord.)
Bong cords () = an ample connection of truths.
Cords () = things that conjoin.
With cord work () = a method of conjunction. A cord = what conjoins.
In the other life there appear cords of varied twist and density, and by them are represented various methods of conjunction; hence cords, in the Word, = things which conjoin. Illustrated.
Cords of vanity () = conjunctions of falsities, through which comes iniquity, or evil of life.
Cords, in the Word, also = portions of inheritances and of land, because the measurements were made by cords. Illustrated.
With cord-work () = indissoluble conjunction. AC 9884. AC 9886.
The cords are plucked away () = that there is no longer any conjunction of good and truth, or of truths among each other. AE 724:16.
Their love is like a bond, or like a cord, with which they are as it were tied round...
They are drawn by their own evil, as by a rope.
Cords, and the snares of death () = temptations, which, being from Hell, are called the cords of Hell.
As a ship's rope cannot pass through the eye of a needle.
(A rope used in punishment.) SE 3979.
A Spirit who had cords, which he extended, to draw his victims into his mouth.
Communication of thoughts and influx is represented by little cords coming down.
To bind with cords () = to conjoin.
To lengthen the cords () = their extension. Cords, here, = their conjunction, AE 799:5. AE 799:10.
